text:
Predicates:
PerformsOften(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
AttendsSchoolEvents(x) ::: x attends and is very engaged with school events.
Student(x) ::: x is a student who attends the school.
ChaperoneHighSchoolDances(x) ::: x chaperones high school dances.
AttendsSchool(x) ::: x attends the school.
InactiveMember(x) ::: x is an inactive and disinterested member of the community.
WishesFurtherCareer(x) ::: x wishes to further their academic careers and educational opportunities.
YoungChildOrTeen(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.

Premises:
∀x (PerformsOften(x) → AttendsSchoolEvents(x)) ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged with school events.
∀x (PerformsOften(x) ∨ (InactiveMember(x))) ::: People either perform in school talent shows often or are inactive and disinterested members of their community.
∀x (ChaperoneHighSchoolDances(x) → ¬AttendsSchool(x)) ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend the school.
∀x (InactiveMember(x) → ChaperoneHighSchoolDances(x)) ::: All people who are inactive and disinterested members of their community chaperone high school dances.
∀x (YoungChildOrTeen(x) ∧ WishesFurtherCareer(x) → Student(x)) ::: All young children and teenagers who wish to further their academic careers and educational opportunities are students who attend the school.
BonnieAttendsAndEngaged ∨ (¬BonnieAttends ∧ ¬BonnieEngaged) ::: Bonnie either both attends and is very engaged with school events and is a student who attends the school, or she neither attends and is very engaged with school events nor is a student who attends the school.

Conclusion:
PerformsOften(Bonnie) ::: Bonnie performs in school talent shows often.
